In other words, still only 1/1000 people suffer from adverse side effects. If the agenda that news site is pushing was fully accepted, it would still be at least an order of magnitude safer to get the vaccine than to live without it.

Even with all that, the agenda the news site is trying to push with that headline and that writing has no evidence so far. Correlation does not imply causation. The only figure they claimed was ~8000 teen girls suffered from some serious illness after getting the HPV vaccine. There was no control, so we have no idea if this is higher or lower than girls who did not get the vaccine. Additionally, they never said how long after the vaccination these illnesses happened. If you get the vaccine and a year later you start having seizures, are they counting that as "serious illness after HPV vaccine"?

Seeing article like this in the MSM shows that the problem can no longer be easily covered up. I preferred the article I read here the other day released by the Danish Govt acknowledging a problem with their HPV vaccine. A very good article and indicative of a greater problem.
3D map of all satellites and debris orbiting the Earth
Why don't we just send a high powered laser up there in parts then assemble it into the final product and start blasting things?

Because there's actually a lot of space in space. While it looks crowded, this is because of how large each object is represented in this graphic, if it was scaled realistically, the entire visualization would be black (except the Earth, obviously), because all the debris would be far smaller than a pixel. There's a lot of stuff up there, yes, but it's really spread out much more than you might think. If functioning spacecraft were getting taken out daily by debris, it would be a different story; and we'd need many time more debris up than they is there now to hit that point.
